desc: Ideation and approach selection (prefer O(n log n) binary lifting for the first implementation)

Implement the O(n log n) binary-lifting two-pointer solution: compute ng[i] = nearest next index with nums[j] > nums[i] using a monotonic stack, prefix sums, and binary lifting tables up[t][i] / contrib[t][i]; define the cost predicate by jumping along ng while landing <= r+1, adding full segment contributions, then adding the final partial segment and comparing against k + sum(nums[l..r]); then for each R advance L while cost(L,R) > k and add R-L+1 to the answer.

Run the current solution on the provided examples and a brute-force O(n^2) checker on small random arrays plus edge cases: n=1, all equal, strictly increasing, strictly decreasing, k=0, and k larger than all costs; report exact pass/fail and any failing cases.
O(n) fallback not required because the O(n log n) solution passed all correctness tests and is within the n=1e5 constraints.
